キックオフミーティング、本当に盛り上げてますか？

「ただ方針を読み上げて終わった…」
「参加者の表情が硬かった…」

キックオフミーティングの進め方と盛り上げる工夫を
10スライドでご紹介

▼ スライド1：盛り上げのコツを体系化

▼ スライド2：目的を明確にする【最重要】
代表的な4つの目的
① 経営方針・目標の全社共有
② チームの一体感・連帯感の醸成
③ 社員のモチベーション向上
④ 新プロジェクトの社内外への宣言

「最も伝えたいこと」を1つ絞る
→ プログラム全体に一貫性が生まれる

▼ スライド3：事前準備①開催形式・会場選定
開催2～3か月前から逆算

【開催形式】
リアル開催＝一体感・熱量重視
オンライン＝全国散在対応
ハイブリッド＝温度差に注意

【会場選択】
普段の会議室より非日常感のある会場
→ 気持ちの切り替え促進
→ 記憶に残りやすい

▼ スライド4：事前準備②プログラム設計
「情報インプット」と「参加型」のバランスが鍵

60～90分に1回は参加者が動けるコーナーを挿入
ワーク・対話・投票で緊張感を維持

【半日4時間プログラムの例】
オープニング映像（5-10分）
経営陣メッセージ（20-30分）
部門別取り組み共有（20-30分）
表彰式（15-20分）
グループワーク（30-45分）
クロージング（10-15分）
懇親会（60分～）

プログラム表を関係者間で共有
→ 準備の抜け漏れを防止

▼ スライド5：オープニング演出【最初が勝負】
① 映像・動画の活用
 ビジョンをビジュアル表現
 ハイライト動画で感情共感

② MCやファシリテーター
 テンポコントロールが重要
 プロに依頼も効果的

③ 入場前から演出
 ウェルカムボード
 席のギフト・メッセージ
 特別なBGM

「この場は特別」と感じさせる工夫

▼ スライド6：盛り上がるコンテンツ①参加型
① チームビルディングワーク
 部署・職種が異なるグループで対話
 「今期、大切な価値観は？」といった問い
 普段接点がない社員がフラットに関われる

② リアルタイム投票・アンケート
 スマートフォン・タブレット活用
 投票結果を即座に表示
 → 会場全体が盛り上がる

▼ スライド7：盛り上がるコンテンツ②表彰・懇親
③ 表彰式の工夫
 受賞者のエピソード・苦労話を動画化
 同僚からのコメント映像を放映
 感動が会場全体に広がる

④ 懇親会・交流タイム
 立食スタイルで動きやすく
 テーブルにゲーム・クイズを配置
 「テーマトーク席」を設定
 自然と会話が生まれる仕掛け

▼ スライド8：オンライン・ハイブリッド開催での工夫
課題：オンライン参加者が傍観者になりやすい

工夫①チャット・リアクション機能を活用
進行役が声かけで場の一部として関わる

工夫②ブレイクアウトルーム
5～6名の小グループで発言しやすく

工夫③共通体験の演出
バーチャル背景の統一・カメラON・リアクション

工夫④映像・音声品質への投資
カメラアングル・照明の調整
事前テストで当日トラブル防止

▼ スライド9：フォローアップと振り返り【決め手】
① ハイライト映像を翌日までに社内配信
 参加者の余韻を持続
 欠席社員にも内容伝達

② 参加者へのアンケート
 「何が印象に残ったか」
 「次回改善してほしい点は」
 → 次回キックオフが見える化

③ 日常業務での定期振り返り
 週次・月次ミーティングで方針を振り返り
 キックオフ内容を繰り返し言及
 社員の行動・意識の変化につながる

▼ スライド10：成功の7ポイント
✅ 目的の明確化
✅ 事前準備の充実
✅ オープニング演出
✅ 参加型コンテンツ
✅ エンゲージメント設計
✅ オンライン対応
✅ フォローアップシステム

Are you truly energizing your kickoff meeting?

"We just read out the policy and it ended..."
"The participants' expressions were stiff..."

We introduce how to conduct a kickoff meeting and ways to energize it in 10 slides.

▼ Slide 1: Systematize the tips for energizing

▼ Slide 2: Clarify the purpose [Most Important]
4 typical purposes:
1. Company-wide sharing of management policy and goals
2. Fostering team unity and a sense of solidarity
3. Improving employee motivation
4. Announcing a new project both internally and externally

Narrow down to "the most important thing to convey"
→ Creates consistency throughout the program

▼ Slide 3: Advance preparation ① Format selection and venue selection
Work backwards from 2 to 3 months before the event

[Event format]
In-person event = Focus on unity and energy
Online = For employees scattered nationwide
Hybrid = Beware of differences in engagement levels

[Venue selection]
Choose a venue with a more extraordinary atmosphere than a typical meeting room
→ Promotes a mental shift
→ Easy to remember

▼ Slide 4: Advance preparation ② Program design
Balance between "information input" and "participation" is key

Insert a segment where participants can move around once every 60 to 90 minutes
Maintain a sense of engagement through workshops, dialogue, and voting

[Example of a half-day 4-hour program]
Opening video (5-10 min)
Management message (20-30 min)
Departmental initiative sharing (20-30 min)
Awards ceremony (15-20 min)
Group work (30-45 min)
Closing (10-15 min)
Social gathering (60 min~)

Share the program table with relevant parties
→ Prevents omissions in preparation

▼ Slide 5: Opening production [The first impression is crucial]
1. Use of images and videos
  Visual representation of the vision
  Emotional engagement through highlight videos

2. MC or facilitator
  Tempo control is important
  Hiring a professional can also be effective

3. Production even before entry
  Welcome board
  Gifts or messages at seats
  Special BGM

Ways to make participants feel "This place is special"

▼ Slide 6: Engaging content ① Participation type
1. Team building workshop
  Dialogue in groups with different departments and roles
  Questions like "What are the important values for this term?"
  Allows employees who usually have no contact to interact on a level playing field

2. Real-time voting and surveys
  Use smartphones and tablets
  Display voting results immediately
  → Excites the entire venue

▼ Slide 7: Engaging content ② Awards and socializing
3. Creative awards ceremony
  Video the recipients' stories and struggles
  Show video comments from colleagues
  Emotion spreads throughout the venue

4. Social gathering / networking time
  Buffet style for easy movement
  Place games and quizzes on tables
  Set up "theme talk seats"
  Mechanisms that naturally generate conversation

▼ Slide 8: Tips for online and hybrid events
Challenge: Online participants tend to become bystanders

Tip 1: Utilize chat and reaction functions
  The facilitator engages them by calling out, making them part of the event

Tip 2: Breakout rooms
  Small groups of 5-6 people make it easier to speak up

Tip 3: Create shared experiences
  Unified virtual backgrounds, cameras ON, reactions

Tip 4: Invest in video and audio quality
  Adjust camera angles and lighting
  Conduct advance tests to prevent issues on the day

▼ Slide 9: Follow-up and review [The Deciding Factor]
1. Distribute highlight videos internally by the next day
  Maintain the participants' lingering excitement
  Also convey the content to absent employees

2. Survey participants
  "What left an impression on you?"
  "What would you like to see improved next time?"
  → Visualizes improvements for the next kickoff

3. Regular review in daily operations
  Review the policy in weekly and monthly meetings
  Repeatedly refer to the kickoff content
  Leads to changes in employee behavior and awareness

▼ Slide 10: 7 Points for Success
✅ Clear purpose
✅ Thorough advance preparation
✅ Opening production
✅ Participatory content
✅ Engagement design
✅ Online support
✅ Follow-up system

Solve your internal event planning concerns with a checklist!

"Problems were discovered on the day itself..."
"I still have concerns about the preparations..."
"I don't know where to start..."

For those in charge with such concerns,
we introduce a 5-phase checklist covering everything from planning to post-event follow-up.

▼ 1: Eliminate preparation anxiety
Prevent omissions with the checklist

▼ 2: Planning Phase
1. Clarify the purpose and goal
  The first step determines quality

2. Determine the target audience and scale
  Decide on the participants and expected number of attendees

3. Select the event format
  Choose from in-person, online, or hybrid

4. Formulate a budget plan
  Identifying expense items and securing a contingency fund are important

5. Set the schedule and assign responsibilities
  Create milestones by working backwards from the event date

▼ 3: Venue and equipment arrangement phase
1. Reserve and contract the venue
  Check capacity, access, and facilities

2. Design the layout
  Choose the seating style (school, theater, banquet)

3. Check audio and video equipment
  Conduct operational tests for microphones, screens, and lighting

4. Arrange food and beverages
  Confirm quantities, allergy accommodations, and serving times

5. Accessibility considerations
  Confirm in advance for wheelchair users and those requiring health-related accommodations

* Venue troubles are often discovered just before the event
  Early confirmation is important!

▼ 4: Attendee recruitment and communication phase
1. Send invitation emails and internal announcements
  Clearly state the date, time, venue, purpose, and items to bring
  Include reminder emails in the plan

2. Manage the participant list
  Track registration status in real time
  Decide in advance how to handle overcapacity or shortfalls

3. Share the day's program
  Distribute the timetable in advance
  Also announce any information requiring preparation beforehand

* Insufficient information sharing leads to lower participation rates

▼ 5: Day-of operation phase
1. Morning setup and equipment check on the day
  Complete 1-2 hours before opening
  Final check of audio, video, and reception environment

2. Brief the staff
  Share assigned areas and emergency contact flow

3. Set up the reception and guidance system
  Clarify name list verification, seating guidance, and baggage handling

4. Assign a timekeeper
  Manage the program to proceed as scheduled

5. Set up a trouble contact point
  Primary contact for equipment issues, health problems, and latecomers

* In preparation for unexpected events,
  scheduling with buffer time is important

▼ 6: Post-event follow-up phase
1. Conduct a survey
  Collect participant feedback promptly
  Design questions aligned with the event's purpose

2. Create a report and minutes
  Summarize event results, budget, number of participants, and outcomes

3. Organize and distribute photos and videos
  Organize and utilize recorded materials from the day

4. Identify areas for improvement
  Based on survey results and reviews
  Document improvement points for the next event

* Handling after the event ends
  leads to quality improvement for the next event

▼ 7: Comprehensive support

Are your preparations for the online general meeting of shareholders going smoothly?

📊 We introduce "8 Key Points for Success" for online general meetings of shareholders.

▼ Do you have these concerns?
・Afraid of streaming issues
・Worried that employees will get bored
・Unsure of the day-of operational structure

▼ What you can do online
✓ Employees nationwide can participate, reducing travel costs
✓ Employees with childcare or caregiving responsibilities can participate more easily
✓ Follow up with employees who could not attend via archives

▼ 3 Environmental settings that determine streaming quality
1. Platform selection
  Thoroughly check interactivity and capacity for the number of participants

2. Network stability is the top priority
  Prepare a wired LAN connection plus a mobile line for backup

3. Equipment setup (camera, microphone, lighting)
  The quality of built-in computer equipment is limited

▼ Program design that captivates viewers
・Create impact with an opening video
・Keep sessions to around 20-30 minutes
・Ensure interactivity with real-time polls, games, and quizzes
・Insert interactive elements throughout

▼ Video production for awards ceremonies and presentation sessions
・Create a visually cohesive space using chroma key compositing
・Emphasize award moments with captions, BGM, and lighting
・Thoroughly capture recipients' reactions on camera
→ There are production techniques possible precisely because it is online

▼ Day-of operational structure [5 essential positions]
1. Streaming operator (manages video and audio switching)
2. MC for program progression (manages program flow and speaker introductions)
3. Chat and Q&A moderator (manages and monitors questions)
4. Technical support specialist (contact point for troubleshooting)
5. Overall director (manages timeline and overall direction)

Clear role division is key to stable operation

▼ Considerations for new employees and remote employees
・Incorporate a new employee introduction session
・Offer forms of participation beyond just speaking
 (Chat reactions, survey responses, etc.)
・Always finish on time to create an environment where people feel free to leave without hesitation

Improving participant engagement
comes from careful attention to detail

▼ Reduce preparation work with comprehensive support
